source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: define prefill/decode ownership, KV placement and eviction, RDMA transfer cost, cache consistency, admission control, failure recovery, and comparison against local or conventional distributed serving. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer: Assume a fixed model, prompt/output distribution, arrival process, GPU/NIC topology and RDMA-capable memory tier; record software, KV precision/layout, sharding, cache capacity, prefill/decode ownership, placement, admission and eviction policy. Define the request KV lifecycle, ownership, versioning and cancellation semantics, and distinguish local, remote-fetch and recompute paths. Hypothesis: at matched workload and quality, disaggregation raises sustained requests/s or reduces decode GPU idle time without worsening TTFT (ms), inter-token latency p99 (ms), RDMA bytes/latency or rejection rate versus local/conventional serving. Inject node/link loss, stale/cancelled requests and migration races; verify no stale KV is consumed and recovery is bounded. Canary limited traffic and fall back to local/recompute on consistency failure, SLO breach, transport fault or capacity instability. Evidence: configs, traces, paired raw samples and fault logs.
